content: 1. Mifepristone increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended. 2. Mitotane decreases the levels of natural progesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of the cytochrome P450 3A4 enzyme, so dosage adjustments may be necessary when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. 3. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Nelfinavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is advised to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. 7. Natural progesterone increases the levels of pomalidomide by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 11. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. 12. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. 13. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Nonhormonal contraceptives are advised. 14. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary if clinically indicated. 16. Natural progesterone increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 17. Natural progesterone increases the levels or effects of topical ruxolitinib by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 18. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism and may alter the levels or effects of natural progesterone. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Stiripentol acts as both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, so co-administered CYP3A4 substrates may require dosage adjustments. 19. Natural progesterone increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, so sensitive CYP3A4 substrates should be monitored for effectiveness when co-administered. 21. Natural progesterone increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates should be avoided, as even minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of the CYP3A substrate according to product labeling. 24. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of natural progesterone by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Vaginal spotting, rash, and edema are potential side effects of progesterone. Use during pregnancy is contraindicated due to hypersensitivity concerns. Progesterone is classified as Pregnancy Category A, meaning controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 26. Diosgenin, derived from Mexican yams (Dioscorea spp.), is a natural source of progesterone.
